title: Tensor-square rho sections have a one-dimensional invariant space
statement:
Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure] and $S$ a semisimple simply connected $F$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme], with semisimple and simply connected defined as in [lem-sfb-rho-section-modules]. Fix a split maximal torus $T\subseteq S$ and a Borel subgroup $B\supseteq T$, and use the character $\rho$, its extension $\widetilde\rho:B\to\mathbf G_m$, and the actual regular-function modules $W_m\subseteq F[S]$ of [lem-sfb-rho-section-modules]. A rational $S$-module is an $F$-vector space $V$ with a coaction $\rho_V:V\to V\otimes_F F[S]$ satisfying the coassociativity and counit identities; $V^S=\{v:\rho_V(v)=v\otimes1\}$. Tensor products have diagonal coaction. All equivariance and invariance below mean identities of coactions, equivalently identities after every commutative $F$-algebra extension. For every integer $m\ge1$,
$$\dim_F (W_m\otimes_F W_m)^S=1.$$
This is the invariant space of the rational group-scheme action, not just invariants of a finite subgroup or of a Lie algebra.

source.place: Lemma 9.7.2(1) and Remark 9.7.3, field version of Seshadri Property I(a), p.247; Alper printed p.49. For R=F[[t]] and the constant group, coefficientwise invariance gives (W_m tensor W_m)^S[[t]]; reduction of its rank-one free module gives the displayed field dimension. Local PDF WANTED; HTML https://arxiv.org/html/1005.2398v3#S9.SS7 read.

proof.text: Fix $m\ge1$ and put $W=W_m$, $\chi=-m\widetilde\rho$ (additive character notation). By [lem-sfb-rho-section-modules], $W$ is nonzero and finite-dimensional; its defining identity is exactly $W=E_B(\chi)$ since $\chi(b)^{-1}=\widetilde\rho(b)^m$. Give $W^\vee=\operatorname{Hom}_F(W,F)$ the contragredient action $(s\ell)(w)=\ell(s^{-1}w)$. This is a rational action: in a basis its matrix is the transpose of the inverse action matrix, obtained by composing regular matrix coefficients with inversion on $S$.

source.place: 22.21--22.22 and 22.29--22.30, printed pp.468--471; agent-written tensor-duality assembly for Alper Lemma 9.7.2(1), field case.

proof.text: There is a linear isomorphism $W\otimes W\to\operatorname{Hom}_F(W^\vee,W)$ taking $u\otimes v$ to $(\ell\mapsto\ell(v)u)$. For a basis $e_i$ and dual basis $e_i^*$ its inverse is $A\mapsto\sum_i A(e_i^*)\otimes e_i$. The two composites are identities by the dual-basis formula. Under conjugation on Hom, $sA(s^{-1}\ell)$ sends a pure tensor to $(\ell\mapsto\ell(sv)su)$, which is the image of $su\otimes sv$. These formulas hold after every scalar extension. Thus invariant tensors correspond exactly to maps satisfying $A(s\ell)=sA(\ell)$, i.e. rational $S$-equivariant maps $W^\vee\to W$.

source.place: 22.21--22.22 and 22.29--22.30, printed pp.468--471; agent-written tensor-duality assembly for Alper Lemma 9.7.2(1), field case.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-rational-induction-character-reciprocity] with $G=S$, $H=B$, $V=W^\vee$ and character $\chi$. The group is affine of finite type, $B$ is closed, and $V$ is finite-dimensional rational by Step 1. Since $E_B(\chi)=W$, it gives $\operatorname{Hom}_S(W^\vee,W)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_B(W^\vee,F_\chi)$. Every linear functional on $W^\vee$ is uniquely evaluation $\ell\mapsto\ell(w)$ at some $w\in W$. Its $B$-equivariance says $\ell(b^{-1}w)=\chi(b)\ell(w)$ for all $\ell$, equivalently $bw=\chi(b)^{-1}w$ after every scalar extension, by separation by a dual basis. Consequently this Hom space is linearly isomorphic to the $B$-eigenvector subspace of $W$ with character $m\widetilde\rho$.

source.place: 22.21--22.22 and 22.29--22.30, printed pp.468--471; agent-written tensor-duality assembly for Alper Lemma 9.7.2(1), field case.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-induced-module-primitive-line] to $E_B(\chi)=W\ne0$. It states that $W^U$ is a line with $T$-weight $w_0\chi$. Because $w_0$ sends the positive roots bijectively to their negatives, $w_0\rho=\frac12\sum_{\alpha\in\Phi^+}w_0\alpha=-\rho$ in the character lattice (equivalently multiply by 2 and cancel in the torsion-free character lattice of the split torus). Hence $w_0\chi=m\rho$. The $B$-eigenvector subspace from Step 3 is exactly this line: eigenvectors are $U$-fixed since $\widetilde\rho|_U=1$; conversely $B=T\ltimes U$ by the multiplication isomorphism in the cited node, so a $U$-fixed vector of $T$-weight $m\rho$ transforms by $m\widetilde\rho$ under $B$. The isomorphisms of Steps 2--3 now identify $(W\otimes W)^S$ with this one-dimensional space, giving the claimed dimension.
